title: Gateway: add Hosted protective throttling mode driven by error budget burn signals
author: Cole Summers
description:
Summary: Adds a new rate-limit mode, "protective throttling", for the Hosted tier that is automatically activated when error budget burn signals indicate elevated risk. This is intended to reduce cascading failures by shedding load early (429 + Retry-After) while we stabilize upstream dependencies (routing/runtime) and to make error budget burn actionable in real time.

Context / motivation: During recent Hosted incidents we observed that error/timeout spikes often precede capacity recovery and lead to feedback loops (retry storms, queue buildup, more timeouts). The tiered SLO + error budget initiative calls for automated mitigation keyed off burn-rate. This PR provides a first mitigation lever at the API gateway by switching to a more conservative rate limiter when burn is high.

Design:
- Adds BudgetSignalClient in gateway that polls the control plane budget endpoint (GET /internal/v1/error-budgets/status) on a short interval with caching and jitter.
- Introduces "protective" limiter profile:
  - AT_RISK: apply per-route token bucket reduction + soft concurrency cap; return 429 with Retry-After; emit x-redwood-protective-throttle: 1.
  - EXHAUSTED: tighter caps + optional per-org global cap; more aggressive 429.
- Guardrails:
  - Hosted-only: protected by request context tier==HOSTED; Dedicated/Private are explicitly excluded.
  - Fail-open: if budget status is unknown/unreachable, do not activate protective throttling.
  - Feature flag: hosted_protective_throttling_enabled (default off) + allowlist by region.
  - Exemptions: health checks + internal control plane traffic are exempt.
- Observability:
  - Adds counters for throttled requests by route/model and by budget state.
  - Adds a gauge for current protective throttle state per region.
  - Adds structured logs when transitioning between OK/AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED.

Operational notes:
- Rollout plan is to enable in warn-only metrics mode (compute/record decisions, but do not enforce) for 48h in us-east, then enforce AT_RISK only, then allow EXHAUSTED mode after validation.
- Runbook link added in gateway oncall docs: "Hosted protective throttling".

Testing:
- Unit tests for budget polling, caching, and state transitions.
- Integration test covering 429 behavior and Retry-After header.
- Load test scenario: verifies limiter switch does not deadlock streaming endpoints.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Wire in multi-window burn rate (5m/1h) directly once burn-rate alerting standard is fully landed (currently using budget risk state computed server-side).
- Console view for protective throttle events and correlation with burn charts.

Risk: Moderate. The default is disabled behind a feature flag; fail-open ensures we don’t accidentally shed traffic due to budget service issues. Potential risk is false positives from stale status; this PR caps staleness and logs transitions for audit.
commits: gateway: introduce BudgetSignalClient w/ cached polling + jitter
gateway: add protective throttle profiles + enforcement path (Hosted only)
gateway: emit metrics/logs for protective throttle state + drops
gateway: add integration tests for 429 + Retry-After
docs: add oncall runbook + config examples
review_conversation:
Peter Holtz: Can we confirm this is fail-open? If budget status endpoint has elevated latency during an incident, we could accidentally make things worse by stalling the gateway.

Cole Summers (author): Yep. BudgetSignalClient has a 200ms timeout and cached last-known-good with a max staleness of 60s. If we have no valid status, we treat it as OK (no protective throttling). Added a metric budget_signal_fetch_failures_total and a log when we fall back.

Aisha Bello: How are we deciding AT_RISK vs EXHAUSTED? I want to ensure we’re not baking burn logic into the gateway since we’re standardizing burn computation elsewhere.

Cole Summers: Gateway consumes a simple enum from control plane (OK/AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED) which is computed by the budget service. No burn math in gateway. I updated naming to match the policy draft and added docs in the config section.

Jordan Lee: Please ensure Dedicated is excluded even if request context is missing tier due to legacy callers. I’d prefer an allowlist: only enable if tier==HOSTED AND hosted flag is enabled.

Cole Summers: Done. The middleware checks hosted_protective_throttling_enabled AND tier==HOSTED. Otherwise it does nothing. Added a regression test where tier is unset.

Amara Diallo: For streaming endpoints, are we throttling on initial request only? We should not tear down active streams.

Cole Summers: Only on request admission. No mid-stream intervention. Also exempted websocket upgrade route used by internal tooling.

Logan Wright: Metrics label cardinality: please avoid org_id on counters. Route/model/region/tier is fine; org_id will explode.

Cole Summers: Agreed. Removed org_id label, kept an optional sampled structured log for forensic debugging when we enter EXHAUSTED.

Aisha Bello: Approving once the staleness cap is in place and we have a clear rollout plan.

Cole Summers: Added maxStalenessSeconds=60 default + rollout steps in description and runbook.

Result: Approved by Aisha, Peter, Jordan, Amara, Logan.
release_notes: - Hosted: add feature-flagged protective throttling in API gateway triggered by error budget risk state (AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED), returning 429 + Retry-After to reduce cascading failures during burn spikes.
